title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). CONCLUSION: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

title: Temporal Changes in Lipoprotein(a) Following Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor generally considered stable over an individual's lifetime. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may transiently alter Lp(a) concentrations, complicating interpretation. We systematically evaluated temporal changes in Lp(a) following ACS. METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review searched MEDLINE and Embase from database inception to February 2026. Eligible studies reported serial Lp(a) measurements at two or more time points after index ACS event. Exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of percent change in mean Lp(a) was performed. RESULTS: Of 3,811 records, 16 studies comprising 1,396 patients met inclusion criteria. Lp(a) demonstrated a dynamic post-ACS trajectory. Using initial post-ACS measurements as the reference, pooled percent change in mean Lp(a) was non-significant at 24 hours post-ACS (+2.5%, 95% CI -6.8 to 11.7; p=0.602). Lp(a) was significantly higher at 7-14 days (+44.0%, 95% CI 4.0-84.1; p=0.031), 1 month (+28.3%, 95% CI 2.7-54.0; p=0.030), and 3-6 months (+22.2%, 95% CI 2.4-42.0; p=0.028). Across two studies, absolute Lp(a) increases >25 nmol/L occurred in 17% and 22% of patients by 3 and 6 months, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) is not static post-ACS. Early post-ACS measurements may underestimate long-term concentrations and risk. Repeat measurement weeks to months later is most informative when initial post-ACS Lp(a) values are near clinical decision thresholds or would influence eligibility for emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies.

title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes. DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume. RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI. METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved). RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77). CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Liver radiomics on routine cardiac CT identifies hepatic stress states that predict heart failure.
abstract: AIMS: Heart failure (HF) prevention remains limited because early multisystem cardiometabolic dysfunction is not captured by conventional risk tools. We evaluated whether liver radiomic phenotypes derived opportunistically from coronary artery calcium computed tomography (CAC-CT) identify imaging-defined hepatic stress states associated with incident HF. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 59 237 individuals undergoing CAC-CT (CLARIFY: 46 028; Houston Methodist: 13 209). Liver regions were segmented and radiomic features extracted to derive a Liver Radiomics Score (LRS). The model was trained in a CLARIFY derivation cohort (Dtr, n = 9205), validated in a hold-out cohort (Dts, n = 36 823), and externally evaluated in Houston Methodist (Dext, n = 13 209). The mean follow-up was 1411 days (SD 760.1) in the pooled Dtr and Dts cohorts (1144 HF events) and 470 days (SD 596) in Dext (212 HF events). Continuous LRS was associated with incident HF [Dts: hazard ratio (HR) 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-1.74; P < 0.001; Dext: HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P = 0.004] and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in Dts. Increasing LRS quartiles showed progressively adverse hepatic, haemodynamic, and cardiometabolic profiles and higher HF risk. Among 17 806 Dts participants with PREVENT data, adding LRS modestly improved discrimination across CAC- and PREVENT-based models (P < 0.001) and improved reclassification metrics (7-year net reclassification improvement up to 0.25; including integrated discrimination improvement up to 0.015). High LRS identified elevated risk in low-risk groups: among participants with CAC=0, high LRS conferred ∼2.5-fold higher 5-year HF incidence, and ∼2.9-fold in PREVENT-low individuals. CONCLUSION: In this large multicentre cohort, liver radiomics from CAC-CT captured hepatic stress states linked to HF risk and modestly improved risk stratification beyond CAC and PREVENT scores.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR. METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs). RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain. METHODS: We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time-varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental-variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory. RESULTS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.5% [95% CI, -1.9% to -1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD -1.6% [95% CI, -2.0% to -0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC-based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap-weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, -0.6% [95% CI, -1.1% to -0.2%]; P=0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC-based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Dialysis Patients: Insights from a Nationwide Registry Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Trans-radial intervention (TRI) has become the standard of care for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, in patients on dialysis, trans-femoral intervention (TFI) remains predominant to preserve upper-limb vessels for arteriovenous fistula despite heightened hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to compare TRI and TFI in dialysis patients undergoing PCI. METHODS: We used the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry to compare patients on dialysis who underwent PCIs with TRI versus TFI from January 2018 to June 2025. An instrumental variable analysis with the institutional proportion of TRI use was performed to assess the risk of access-site bleeding and other peri-procedural outcomes. RESULTS: Among 137,702 dialysis patients who underwent PCI, 28.3% of patients underwent TRI (n=38,901), while 71.7% patients underwent TFI (n=98,801). TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding at the access site (adjusted risk difference [aRD]: -0.35%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.56% to -0.15%). Overall bleeding (aRD: -1.38%; 95% CI: -1.89% to -0.87%), access-site hematoma (aRD: -0.86%; 95% CI: -1.13% to -0.60%), myocardial infarction (aRD: -0.21%; 95% CI: -0.39% to -0.03%), and mortality (aRD: -1.07%; 95% CI: -1.64% to -0.51%) were also less frequently observed in TRI. Conversely, TRI was associated with a higher risk of stroke (aRD: 0.23%; 95% CI: 0.001% to 0.45%), driven primarily by ischemic stroke. CONCLUSIONS: TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding events, but the effect size was modest. The higher observed stroke risk highlights a potential ischemic trade-off and warrants further study.

title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts. METHODS: A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated. RESULTS: The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM. CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation revisited: Early entrenchment of AF episodes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 7-day threshold defining persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is clinically entrenched but biologically arbitrary. Whether episode termination follows scale-free dynamics or time-dependent entrenchment remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the probability of spontaneous termination and assess its dependence on episode duration using large-scale pacemaker monitoring. METHODS: Continuous pacemaker monitoring data from the ACaSA study were analyzed. Device-detected AF episodes were reconstructed from daily burden using predefined continuity rules. Termination was modelled as the conditional probability that an ongoing episode would terminate within the subsequent 24 hours. Duration dependence was assessed using a shared frailty Weibull survival model, and episode duration distributions were compared using the Vuong likelihood-ratio test. RESULTS: After excluding patients with single-chamber devices or 100% baseline AF burden, 251 of 281 pacemaker recipients contributed 204,775 patient-days. Device-detected AF occurred in 154 patients, who contributed 7002 reconstructed episodes. Termination probability declined from 91.1% at 1 hour to 72.1% at 12 hours, 33.3% at 24 hours, and 4.3% at 7 days. Episode durations were better described by a lognormal distribution than by a scale-free power-law model. CONCLUSION: Device-detected AF episodes show marked early entrenchment, with spontaneous termination becoming progressively less likely as episode duration increases. These findings support the concept that "AF begets AF" even at short timescales and suggest that persistence beyond 24 hours identifies a state with a substantially reduced likelihood of near-term spontaneous termination. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05127720. GOV ID: NCT05127720.

title: Incremental yield of genetic retesting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Modern genetic testing in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) includes newly described HCM-associated genes and full intronic regions of certain classic sarcomeric genes. This study evaluated genetic retesting in HCM patients with a prior negative test and identified predictors of a positive result to guide retesting. METHODS: This multicentre study included patients with HCM who previously had negative next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based genetic testing at four centres. Subjects were retested using an updated NGS-based HCM panel. RESULTS: Of 508 retested HCM patients (median age 70 years; 66.9% male; median maximal left ventricular wall thickness 18 mm; median interval from initial genetic test 6.6 years), 46 (9%) had 48 HCM-related variants: 14 in new HCM-associated genes, 3 in deep intronic MYBPC3 regions, 18 intermediate-effect variants, and 13 (8 reclassified) in classic HCM-associated genes. In multivariable analysis, the presence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) [odds ratio (OR) 3.52; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-10.25], the Mayo HCM score (OR 1.46 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-2.01), and the Toronto HCM score (OR 1.18 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-1.30) were independent predictors of detecting HCM-related variants at retesting. The diagnostic yields in patients with LGE and a high Toronto score (≥13 points), and with LGE and a high Mayo score (≥4 points), were 80% and 50%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HCM and prior negative genetic testing, retesting identified HCM-related variants in 9% of individuals, allowing counselling and risk stratification. Late gadolinium enhancement, combined with the Mayo and Toronto scores, may be used to guide which patients should be prioritized for genetic retesting.

title: Cardiovascular outcomes with survodutide in adults with obesity at increased cardiovascular risk (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Survodutide, a glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, improved markers of cardiometabolic health in people with obesity, but cardiovascular safety for this new class remains to be established. METHODS: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT was a global, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre, event-driven, cardiovascular safety trial conducted at 524 clinical sites in 34 countries. We included participants aged 18 years or older with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater and established cardiovascular disease or at least two obesity complications or risk factors for cardiovascular disease; participants with chronic kidney disease were eligible if they also had a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. Participants were randomly assigned by interactive response technology (1:1:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (up-titrated to 3·6 mg or 6·0 mg) or placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event (targeting 189 primary endpoint events). We assessed the non-inferiority of pooled survodutide compared with placebo with a margin of 1·65 for the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio (HR). Efficacy and safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of survodutide or placebo. The primary analysis was performed according to the treatment-regimen estimand, which assessed treatment effects regardless of any early discontinuation of survodutide or placebo, temporary stop, the use of protocol-prohibited obesity medications, or a prolonged dose-escalation period. This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06077864. FINDINGS: From Nov 20, 2023, to Nov 8, 2024, we screened 7753 participants, of whom 5530 (71·3%) participants were recruited and randomly assigned to treatment. 23 (0·4%) participants were not treated; 1836 (33·3%) of 5507 participants received survodutide 3·6 mg, 1835 (33·3%) received 6·0 mg, and 1836 (33·3%) received placebo; 2194 (39·8%) were female, 3313 (60·2%) were male, and 4332 (78·7%) were White. Median time in study was 22·0 months (IQR 20·1-23·7). 1029 (56·0%) in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 1039 (56·6%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg group, and 1083 (59·0%) in the placebo group remained on treatment until study closeout. The primary endpoint occurred in 136 (3·7%) of 3671 participants in the survodutide group and in 76 (4·1%) 1836 participants in the placebo group (HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·67-1·18; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Adverse events occurred in 1708 (93·0%) of 1836 participants with survodutide 3·6 mg, 1708 (93·1%) of 1835 with survodutide 6·0 mg, and 1571 (85·6%) of 1836 with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with survodutide than in the placebo group (nausea occurred in 882 [48·0%] of 1836 participants in the 3·6 mg group and 900 [49·0%] of 1835 in the 6·0 mg group vs 223 [12·1%] of 1836 in the placebo group, and vomiting occurred in 582 [31·7%] participants in the 3·6 mg group and 623 [34·0%] in the 6·0 mg group vs 89 [4·8%] in the placebo group). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations occurred in 354 (19·3%) participants in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 (20·8%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 34 (1·9%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates across treatment groups (413 [22·5%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 [20·8%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 439 [23·9%] in the placebo group). Fatal adverse events were similar across treatment groups (16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 11 [0·6%] in the placebo group) and were primarily due to cardiac disorders (six [0·3%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, seven [0·4%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and six [0·3%] in the placebo group). INTERPRETATION: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. This cardiovascular safety trial provides clinicians with reassuring data that treatment with survodutide, a novel glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk. FUNDING: Boehringer Ingelheim.

title: Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication. METHODS: A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy. RESULTS: The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy. CONCLUSIONS: Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

title: A transient modified mRNA encoding Myc and cyclin T1 improves cardiac function after myocardial injury.
abstract: Myc is an evolutionarily conserved transcription factor that is necessary for the restoration of tissues in multiple regenerative species. The adult mammalian heart lacks regenerative capacity and cardiomyocytes fail to divide following damage-induced signaling. Transgenic expression of Myc and cyclin T1 can drive substantial adult cardiomyocyte proliferation to replace lost cardiomyocytes. Here, using transgenic models and a prototypical mRNA therapeutic, we show that Myc and cyclin T1 require transient induction for cardiomyocyte proliferation that leads to myocardial repair and functional recovery after myocardial infarction in mice. This research provides a strategy to translate Myc-cyclin T1 coexpression for cardiac regeneration to address serious unmet needs in the treatment of cardiovascular disease.

title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status. METHODS: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status. RESULTS: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

title: SUDDEN CARDIAC ARREST IN NEW SOUTH WALES (NSW), AUSTRALIA: A DATA LINKAGE STUDY.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a global health challenge. Routinely collected health data represents a potential source of data to identify SCA. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate whether routinely collected health data can retrospectively identify community-based SCA (1-50 years) in NSW. METHODS: Potential SCA cases (aged 1-50yrs; occurring in NSW; cardiac-related ICD-9/10/SNOMED codes) were identified by the Centre for Health Record Linkage (CHeReL) in the NSW Ambulance OHCA Register (OHCAR) and NSW Emergency Department Data Collection (EDDC). Probabilistic data linkage was undertaken between ambulance, hospital and mortality datasets. External causes were excluded at case identification in ambulance records. Cardiac aetiology was assigned where a cardiac diagnosis appeared in hospital admission or cause of death records. RESULTS: From 1.7 million linked records, 13,345 presumed SCA cases were identified; 54% had cardiac aetiology and 83% were fatal. Cardiac cases were older than non-cardiac cases (median 42 vs 37 years, p < 0.001) and more likely to be admitted to hospital (58% vs 7%, p < 0.001). Within cardiac cases, rhythm-related and structural diagnoses dominated in 1-11 year olds, while ischaemic disease dominated in 35-50 year olds. Older cardiac cases were more likely to die pre-hospital (adjusted OR 3.56, 95% CI 2.66-4.85, for 35-50 vs 1-11 years). CONCLUSIONX: Multi-source administrative data linkage identifies age-related patterns in SCA aetiology and clinical trajectory. Findings extrapolated nationally suggest approximately 370 cardiac SCA deaths per year in Australians aged 1 to 35, a substantial burden that could be tracked through routine data linkage.

title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

title: Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US. OBSERVATIONS: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

title: Tirofiban Prevents Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Aged Mice.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvasculature has been demonstrated in animal models of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) as well as autopsy studies of patients with aneurysmal SAH, and microthrombi are thought to contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia and poor neurological outcomes. Our hypothesis was that treatment with tirofiban, an antiplatelet drug that inhibits glycoprotein IIb/IIIa, would reduce microthrombi formation and the subsequent sequalae, delayed cerebral ischemia, in aged mice. METHODS: SAH was induced via endovascular perforation in male mice, and blood injection in female mice, followed by treatment with either tirofiban or saline. Mice underwent daily neurological assessment for 6 days and then were euthanized. Magnetic resonance imaging scans were obtained on days 2, 4, and 6 after SAH to identify infarcted tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging perfusion and laser speckle contrast imaging were performed to evaluate cerebral perfusion. Postmortem microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvascular was quantified. RESULTS: Tirofiban treatment in male mice, compared with saline, led to reduced microthrombi formation, and prevented delayed infarct growth and neurological decline. In female mice, significant neurobehavioral improvements were observed, which corresponded with fewer brain microthrombi. No female mice had infarction, nor was delayed cerebral ischemia detected in any female mouse. CONCLUSIONS: After SAH in mice, treatment with tirofiban reduces both cerebral microthrombi formation and delayed infarct growth leading to a subsequent improvement in neurological outcomes.

title: Endothelial KLK8 Promotes Diabetic Nephropathy via a LIFR Dependent Mechanism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The molecular pathways in endothelial cells (ECs) in diabetic nephropathy (DN), a primary microvascular complication of diabetes, remain unclear. Tissue KLKs (kallikrein-related peptidases) participate in pathophysiological processes in ECs. We aimed to explore the roles of endothelial KLKs in DN and define the underlying mechanisms. METHODS AND RESULTS: Renal KLK8 was the most highly upregulated KLK in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice and cultured glomerular ECs (GECs) upon high glucose treatment. C57/BL6 background global (Klk8-/-) and endothelial Klk8 knockout (Klk8ΔEC) mice, as well as DBA/2J mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown, displayed improved albuminuria, mesangial matrix expansion, and glomerulosclerosis caused by streptozotocin compared with the corresponding wild-type mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed that many pathways linked to DN in ECs, mesangial cells, and tubule cells were reversed in Klk8ΔEC mice. Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition caused by streptozotocin was extensively improved in Klk8ΔEC mice, which was confirmed in Cdh5CreERT2+/--mT/mG+/- mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown. Proteome coupled with other approaches revealed that KLK8 cleaved SDC4 (syndecan-4), which contributed to the loss of glycocalyx integrity in GECs during DN progress. Lifr was one of the key genes in ECs and mesangial cells regulated by endothelial Klk8 during DN progress. Endothelial KLK8 upregulated LIFR (leukemia inhibitory factor receptor) expression through PLC (phospholipase C)/ERK (extracellular signal-regulated kinase)/RUNX1 (runt-related transcription factor)1 pathways, and upregulated LIFR contributed to high glucose-induced GEC dysfunction and MC activation. Knockdown of Lifr ameliorated hallmark features of DN and improved endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and SDC4 expression in the glomeruli of diabetic mice. LIFR was upregulated in GECs and mesangial cells in patients with DN. Circulatory LIF (leukemia inhibitory factor), KLK8 and soluble SDC4 levels were increased in patients with DN, and KLK8 level was positively correlated with LIF, soluble SDC4 and creatinine levels. CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial KLK8 promotes GEC dysfunction and abnormal crosstalk with mesangial cells through a LIFR-dependent signaling in DN, which immediately highlights therapeutic targets for DN.

title: Multiple Traumas Accelerate the Transition From Cardiovascular Disease to Depression: A Multistate Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumas are risk factors for both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depression. However, the specific impacts of trauma on the critical transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression and mortality remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the UK Biobank cohort (N=138 036), we constructed multistate models to investigate the associations of childhood trauma, adult trauma, and lifetime trauma with the transitions between health states. Specifically, we modeled transitions from a healthy state to incident CVD, further to subsequent depression, and ultimately to death. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 14 278 participants developed incident CVD, with 679 developed subsequent depression and 4144 dying. Trauma was positively associated with the dynamic disease progression: the transition from baseline to incident CVD showed significantly elevated hazards for multiple childhood traumas (hazard ratio [HR], 1.294 [95% CI, 1.170-1.432]), adult traumas (HR, 1.145 [95% CI, 1.071-1.225]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.632 [95% CI, 1.528-1.742]) compared with no trauma exposure. Similarly, the transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression demonstrated increased risks for multiple childhood traumas (HR, 2.260 [95% CI, 1.661-3.075]), adult traumas (HR, 1.950 [95% CI, 1.510-2.518]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.608 [95% CI, 1.245-2.078]) versus no trauma exposure. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that exposure to multiple traumas significantly increases the risk of developing depression following an incident CVD diagnosis. This underscores the urgent need for clinical and public health interventions targeting multiple traumas to mitigate the risk of CVD and depression progression, thereby improving outcomes.

title: Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis. METHODS: Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points. RESULTS: Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels. METHODS: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change). RESULTS: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer.
abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor-host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I-IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility.

title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors. RESULTS: In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models. CONCLUSIONS: Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

title: Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid weight loss, as induced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, is accompanied by pronounced muscle loss. GDF8 (myostatin) and activin A (ActA), acting via ActRIIA/B receptors, are negative regulators of muscle mass. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antibodies blocking GDF8 (trevogrumab) and ActA (garetosmab) on semaglutide-induced weight and muscle loss. METHODS: COURAGE is a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial. This multicentre (60 sites), US-based trial enrolled participants aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). In part A, participants were treated for 26 weeks with semaglutide (titrated to 2·4 mg subcutaneously weekly) in addition to a randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) concomitant treatment: placebo, trevogrumab 200 mg, trevogrumab 400 mg, or trevogrumab 400 mg and garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Trevogrumab was administered subcutaneously weekly and garetosmab was administered intravenously every 4 weeks. Part A also included a subsequent semaglutide withdrawal period, at which point participants (randomly assigned at baseline 1:1 within each group) received either trevogrumab 400 mg or placebo for an additional 26 weeks. In part B, participants were treated with semaglutide for 52 weeks and randomly assigned (1:2:2) to concomitant treatment with placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. Groups were stratified according to sex, BMI (<35 kg/m2vs ≥35 kg/m2), and participation in an exploratory MRI substudy assessing thigh muscle volume. Study participants, the principal investigators, and study site personnel were masked to all randomisation assignments throughout the study. Primary endpoints were percent change in lean mass, fat mass, and bodyweight from baseline to week 26 (part A) or week 52 (part B). Efficacy and safety analyses were done in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of a study drug (efficacy, as randomly assigned; safety, as treated). COURAGE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299098, and is currently active, not recruiting. FINDINGS: 975 participants were enrolled between June 21, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Mean age was 49·0 years (SD 13·2) and mean BMI was 36·7 kg/m2 (SD 5·0); 627 (64%) of 975 participants were female and 348 (36%) were male. In part A (n=605, of whom n=599 received at least one dose of study drug), a substantial decrease in lean mass was observed in the semaglutide plus placebo group at week 26 (-6·6% [95% CI -7·4 to -5·7]); the estimated treatment difference (ETD) versus semaglutide plus placebo was +3·1% (95% CI 1·9 to 4·3) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg, +2·7% (1·5 to 4·0) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg, and +4·5% (3·1 to 5·9) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg. In part B (n=376), lean mass percent change from baseline to week 52 for semaglutide plus placebo was -7·3% (-8·8 to -5·8); the ETD versus semaglutide plus placebo was +1·5% (-0·3 to 3·3) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 25 mg, and +3·1% (1·3 to 4·9) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 75 mg. Change from baseline in fat mass in part A was -15·6% (-17·4 to -13·9) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg group (-3·4% [-5·9 to -0·9]) and the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-11·7% [-14·4 to -9·0]) in part A. No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in fat mass compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Percent change in bodyweight in part A was -10·6 (-11·6 to -9·7) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant for the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-2·7 [-4·1 to -1·2]). No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in bodyweight compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Semaglutide plus trevogrumab (25 mg, 75 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) was generally well tolerated with a safety profile similar to semaglutide plus placebo; however, semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg had a high incidence of serious adverse events (14 [9%] of 149) and treatment discontinuations (48 [32%] of 149). Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most commonly reported, and they occurred with similar incidence across treatment groups. Muscle spasms occurred more frequently in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (61 [41%] of 149) compared with the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg or 400 mg groups (23 [8%] of 299) and semaglutide plus placebo groups (seven [5%] of 151). Most adverse events were mild to moderate in severity. Two deaths occurred during the study, both in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group; a causal association between treatment and these events was not identified. INTERPRETATION: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health. FUNDING: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

title: Modified Posterior Wall Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: the BOX-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: AIMS: The efficacy of left atrial posterior wall isolation (PWI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is controversial. We propose a modified left atrial posterior wall ablation strategy. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of modified posterior wall ablation in patients with persistent AF who underwent first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicenter, single-blind randomized trial, 276 patients with persistent AF were assigned 1:1 to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) with (BOX+) or without modified posterior wall ablation (BOX-). Seven participants withdrew, leaving 269 (BOX+, n=139; BOX-, n=130) for primary endpoint analysis. The primary endpoint was freedom from any documented atrial arrhythmia lasting > 30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs after a 3 -month blanking period. At 12-month follow-up, the primary endpoint occurred in 120 of 139 patients (86.3%) in the BOX+ group and 113 of 130 (86.9%) in the BOX- group (hazard ratio 1.046, 95% CI, 0.54 - 2.01; P = 0.894). The BOX+ group exhibited longer procedure time and ablation time. Acute successful PWI was achieved in 91 (65.5%) patients assigned to BOX+. In a nonprespecified, post-randomization analysis, arrhythmia-free survival was 93.4% in patients with acute successful PWI, 72.9% in those with attempted but unsuccessful PWI, and 86.9% in controls without attempted PWI (overall log-rank P=0.002). Adverse events were similar between groups. CONCLUSION: Routine addition of modified posterior wall ablation did not improve overall outcomes of first-time ablation in persistent AF. However, achieving successful PWI was associated with significantly lower recurrence.

title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. Diet is a key modifiable determinant of gut microbiome composition and metabolic output, yet its role in post-stroke neuroplasticity has not been comprehensively synthesized. This narrative review examines dietary interventions with mechanistic or translational relevance to ischemic stroke recovery, including Mediterranean dietary patterns, ketogenic diets, high-fiber and prebiotic-enriched diets, probiotic and synbiotic supplementation, and intermittent fasting or caloric restriction. We summarize evidence linking diet-induced microbiome modulation to neuroinflammatory regulation, short-chain fatty acid signaling, microglial activity, mitochondrial function, and synaptic plasticity. Shared and diet-specific pathways are discussed, along with current limitations of the evidence base and barriers to clinical translation. Collectively, available data support a biologically plausible role for targeted dietary modulation of the gut microbiome as an adjunctive strategy to enhance cognitive recovery and neuroplasticity after ischemic stroke. Further well-designed clinical studies integrating microbiome profiling, neuroimaging, and cognitive outcomes are needed to define therapeutic potential and guide implementation in stroke rehabilitation. Among these dietary interventions, Mediterranean, high-fiber, and prebiotic-enriched diets currently have the strongest available evidence, while ketogenic and intermittent fasting approaches remain the least supported based on existing clinical and translational evidence.

title: Piezo1 Responsiveness in Muscle Afferents and Mechanoreflex in Diabetic Rats.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abnormal mechanoreflex function from skeletal muscle significantly contributes to the heightened circulatory response during exercise in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that the abnormal cardiovascular responses in T2DM are mediated by mechanoreflex-induced exaggerations resulting from enhanced Piezo1-mediated mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents. METHODS: T2DM rats (Sprague-Dawley rats) were given a high-fat diet in combination with a low dose of streptozotocin. Using an in vivo decerebrated rat model and an ex vivo single-fiber recording preparation, we measured muscle mechanoreflex responses, mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents, and Piezo1-mediated responses. Piezo1 protein levels in the membrane fraction were detected by Western blotting in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells. RESULTS: Blood pressure and sympathetic nerve activity responses to mechanoreflex activation, as well as group IV muscle afferent firing to mechanical stimulation and the Piezo1 agonist (Yoda1), were significantly greater in T2DM rats. More importantly, Piezo1 agonist-induced blood pressure changes and group IV afferent firing were significantly potentiated by administration of lipopolysaccharide, a gut-derived inflammatory endotoxin. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide significantly increased Piezo1 protein in the cell membrane, which was attenuated by a PKA (protein kinase A) inhibitor. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that activation of the lipopolysaccharide-Piezo1 pathway may contribute to enhanced responsiveness of group IV muscle afferents and may be associated with exaggerated circulatory responses to muscle mechanoreflex activation in T2DM.

title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype. METHODS: This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events. RESULTS: Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P<0.05). No significant functional benefit was observed in the LAA group of mRS 0 or 1 (aOR, 0.91; P=0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P=0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P=0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype (P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P=0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P=0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain. METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

title: High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors.
