Given rising use and increasing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

title: Sacubitril/valsartan for radiation-induced heart disease in children: preclinical and clinical findings.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a life-threatening sequela for cancer survivors. A proactive preventive strategy is urgently needed but remains elusive, particularly for the vulnerable paediatric population where prospective data are scarce. To address this gap, this study aimed to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan against RIHD in children through a comprehensive translational research pipeline. METHODS: A prospective observational study was first conducted in 40 paediatric solid tumour patients, comparing cardiac function before and 1 week after radiotherapy, with 80 healthy controls. A juvenile rat RIHD model was then established, in which the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan was assessed and validated through longitudinal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, bulk RNA-seq, and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Finally, a prospective clinical cohort (n = 15 sacubitril/valsartan, n = 15 control) was conducted in paediatric patients post-radiotherapy, with a 12-month follow-up for efficacy and safety. RESULTS: In paediatric patients, radiotherapy significantly impaired biventricular function, notably reducing left ventricular global longitudinal strain, and mean heart radiation dose was significantly correlated with cardiac function impairment. In juvenile rats, sacubitril/valsartan attenuated pathological ventricular wall thickening, myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and perfusion deficits. Mechanistically, it mitigated endothelial cell damage and immune cell activation, promoted a macrophage phenotypic shift from M1 to M2, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and broadly attenuated pro-fibrotic and inflammatory cell-cell communication. In the clinical cohort, sacubitril/valsartan significantly improved left ventricular global longitudinal strain and aortic compliance vs controls, with a favourable safety profile. CONCLUSIONS: This first-in-kind translational study demonstrates that early prophylaxis with sacubitril/valsartan is a feasible and effective strategy to mitigate radiation-induced cardiotoxicity in children. These findings, underpinned by multi-modal validation from bench to bedside, challenge the reactive management paradigm in paediatric cardio-oncology and establish a foundational evidence base for a new standard of proactive heart care in childhood cancer survivors.

title: Inflammation and early atherosclerosis beyond traditional risk factors: an imaging study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Understanding how inflammation contributes to subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) plaque burden, beyond the impact of established cardiovascular risk factors, holds significant implications for the success of preventive strategies focused on the reduction of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The aim of this study was to investigate the relative contribution of inflammation, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDLc), and systolic blood pressure (SBP), as determinants of SA plaque burden in a cohort of middle-aged, asymptomatic individuals, using non-invasive imaging techniques. METHODS: Participants from the Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis (PESA) study (median age 45 years) underwent longitudinal screening every 3 years (baseline, 3- and 6-year visits) involving serial blood testing [including white blood cell (WBC) count, fibrinogen, oxidized LDLc, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein], physical examinations and imaging assessments with three-dimensional vascular ultrasound of peripheral arteries, and coronary artery calcium quantification. Global plaque volume (GPV, mm3; bilateral carotid plus femoral plaque burden) at 6-year follow-up was the primary outcome. Multivariable linear regression and proportional odds models determined the link of GPV to both inflammatory markers and established cardiovascular risk factors. RESULTS: Of the 3471 participants, 58% had SA (GPV >0 mm3) at 6-year follow-up. WBC count had the strongest statistical associations with 6-year SA burden after adjusting for age, sex, baseline LDLc, and mean SBP, with an estimated 32.6% increase in GPV per one standard deviation (SD) increase in WBC (Z = 7.33, P < 1 × 10-10). GPV at 6 years increased 40.9% per one SD increase in baseline LDLc and 42.7% per one SD increase in mean SBP (Z = 8.80 and Z = 7.97, respectively, both P < 1 × 10-10; their SDs were 29.4 mg/dL and 11.5 mmHg, respectively), followed by fibrinogen (16.8% increase in GPV per one SD increase, Z = 3.91, P < .0001). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was not predictive of greater GPV at 6 years (Z = 1.36, P = .174). For WBC, the marked trend in risk occurred only at levels above its median. Similar patterns were observed for separate analyses of carotid and femoral plaque volumes, and coronary artery calcium. Increasing levels of WBC and fibrinogen were also associated with a greater anatomical spread of disease. CONCLUSIONS: Inflammation contributes to SA burden, as assessed by direct plaque quantification, beyond the effects of LDLc and SBP. These findings indicate that inflammation, captured through the use of systemic inflammatory markers, is a risk factor relevant across the entire continuum of atherosclerosis, exerting a deleterious impact comparable to that of LDLc and SBP.

title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses. METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

title: Association of Stroke Severity With Efficacy of Early Tirofiban Infusion After Intravenous Thrombolysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to assess the effects of stroke severity at admission on the efficacy and safety of early tirofiban infusion following intravenous thrombolysis in patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke using data from the ASSET-IT (Advancing Stroke Safety and Efficacy Through Early Tirofiban Administration After Intravenous Thrombolysis) trial. METHODS: All 832 patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke from the ASSET-IT database were included in this exploratory post hoc analysis. The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were an excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days) and intracranial hemorrhage. RESULTS: Among the 832 patients included, the median age was 69 (interquartile range, 59-76) years, 531 (63.8%) were men, 367 (44.1%) had minor stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6), and 465 (55.9%) had moderate-to-severe stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥6). There were significant interactions between the primary efficacy and safety outcomes (Pinteraction=0.008, Pinteraction=0.03; respectively). We observed that among patients with NIHSS score ≥6, tirofiban markedly increased odds of achieving an excellent functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.44-3.17]; P<0.001) without significantly increasing the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.37-2.09]; P=0.77). In contrast, no significant benefit was observed in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6 group (adjusted odds ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.64-1.63]; P=0.94) but there was a significant increase in the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 6.51 [95% CI, 1.42-62.03]; P=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Early tirofiban infusion may be more beneficial for patients with moderate-to-severe stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset, while simultaneously suggesting an increased potential risk of intracranial hemorrhage in minor stroke. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06134622.

title: Intraoperative Hypotension and Risk of Cuff Blood Pressure Inaccuracy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension is associated with cardiovascular complications and mortality, making accurate blood pressure (BP) monitoring essential. However, the accuracy of noninvasive oscillometric cuff BP (Cuff BP) during hypotension is uncertain. We examined the association between intraoperative hypotension and Cuff BP inaccuracy. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort included 22 812 adults undergoing noncardiac surgery from April 2013 through November 2023, with 348 888 simultaneous Cuff BP and invasive arterial BP (Arterial BP) pairs. Pairs with arterial systolic BP >120 mm Hg or diastolic BP >80 mm Hg were excluded to focus on the hypotensive range. Hypotension was defined as arterial mean arterial pressure (MAP)<65 mm Hg and categorized as mild (55 to <65), moderate (45 to <55), or severe (35 to <45 mm Hg). Cuff BP inaccuracy was defined as an absolute MAP difference >10 mm Hg from Arterial BP. Multivariable generalized estimating equation models estimated adjusted odds ratios and 95% CIs. RESULTS: Compared with normal MAP (≥65 mm Hg), hypotension was associated with higher odds of Cuff BP inaccuracy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 [95% CI, 1.40-1.50]). Adjusted odds ratios increased with severity (P value for trend <0.001): 1.28 (95% CI, 1.24-1.32) for mild, 2.33 (95% CI, 2.20-2.46) for moderate, and 7.00 (95% CI, 6.13-8.00) for severe hypotension. Sensitivity for correct MAP classification decreased from 87.4% for normal MAP to 32.6%, 20.2%, and 9.6% for mild, moderate, and severe hypotension. CONCLUSIONS: We found a significantly higher risk of Cuff BP inaccuracy in patients with intraoperative hypotension, supporting cautious interpretation of Cuff BP during intraoperative hypotension.

title: Skeletal Muscle sEVs Mediate Exercise-Induced Cardioprotection in I/R Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise training has been demonstrated to provide direct endogenous cardioprotection and to reduce cardiovascular disease risk. Skeletal muscle functions not only as an organ for movement but also as a vital secretory organ. However, how muscle-heart crosstalk contributes to exercise-induced cardioprotection remains largely unclear. Here, we investigated the cardioprotective effects of exercise-induced small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from skeletal muscle in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury in mice. METHODS: An adeno-associated virus 8-dMCK (double-muscle creatine kinase)-CD63-EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein) reporter system was used to track skeletal muscle-derived sEVs in the heart of mice after 4 weeks of exercise. To determine whether sEVs from exercised skeletal muscle mediate cardioprotection, cardiac sEV abundance was increased by intramyocardial injection and decreased by generating skeletal muscle-specific Rab27a knockout mice. The molecular mechanism was elucidated by profiling sEV-enriched microRNAs and validating their functions in cardiomyocytes and mouse MI/R injury models. The translational potential was then assessed in human exercise cohorts. Finally, the therapeutic efficacy was evaluated using miRNA agomirs and adeno-associated virus 8-mediated, skeletal muscle-specific overexpression of miRNAs in MI/R injury models. RESULTS: Exercise promoted the entry of skeletal muscle-derived sEVs into the heart. Skeletal muscle-derived sEVs from exercised mice significantly attenuated MI/R injury by reducing cardiomyocyte apoptosis and improving mitochondrial respiration. Exercise-mediated protection against MI/R injury was attenuated after inhibiting the secretion of sEVs from skeletal muscle. Mechanistically, exercise-enriched sEVs delivered miR-451a and miR-143-3p to cardiomyocytes, thereby modulating the PERK (protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase)-ATF4-CHOP stress-response pathway and the USP46/P53 axis, thus reducing cardiomyocyte death. Skeletal muscle-specific overexpression of miR-451a/143-3p recapitulated the cardioprotective effects of exercise in vivo. Furthermore, exercising humans also showed elevated levels of miR-451a/143-3p in their skeletal muscle and circulating sEVs. CONCLUSIONS: Our study reveals a novel exercise-induced cardioprotective mechanism via muscle-heart crosstalk, highlighting a promising therapeutic approach for treating cardiovascular disease.

title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored. METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA. RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08). CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

title: Rationale and Design of a Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial: LEAP-Block.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited. METHODS: The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications. CONCLUSIONS: The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

title: ZEB1-Driven GLS1 Transcription Promotes Macrophage Glutamine Metabolism in PAH.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The transcriptional mechanisms governing macrophage glutamine metabolism in pulmonary arterial hypertension remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of ZEB1 (zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1)-mediated transcriptional regulation in macrophage metabolic reprogramming and the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension. METHODS: Clinical samples and multiomics data sets were analyzed to characterize ZEB1 expression in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 conditional knockout mice were subjected to hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension. Transcriptomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and coimmunoprecipitation were integrated to define ZEB1-dependent molecular, metabolic, and inflammatory programs in pulmonary and bone marrow-derived macrophages. Therapeutic potential was further evaluated using pharmacological interventions and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing in monocrotaline-induced pulmonary hypertension in rats. RESULTS: ZEB1 was upregulated in pulmonary arterial hypertension and enriched in recruited disease-associated macrophages. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 deletion attenuated macrophage inflammation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and right ventricular dysfunction. Mechanistically, ZEB1 bound the GLS (glutaminase) promoter and recruited BRD4 (bromodomain-containing protein 4), enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation at the GLS promoter and promoting GLS transcription and glutamine metabolic reprogramming. Restoration of GLS partially reversed the metabolic and inflammatory effects of ZEB1 deficiency. Pharmacological targeting of ZEB1, combined BRD4 and GLS inhibition, and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing ameliorated experimental pulmonary hypertension. CONCLUSIONS: ZEB1 promotes macrophage glutamine metabolic reprogramming by recruiting BRD4 and enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation-dependent GLS transcription. This ZEB1-driven metabolic program promotes macrophage inflammation and pulmonary vascular remodeling, identifying the ZEB1-BRD4-GLS regulatory axis as a potential therapeutic target in pulmonary arterial hypertension.

title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH. METHODS: We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete. FINDINGS: Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]). INTERPRETATION: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH. FUNDING: Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, 72-week clinical trial was conducted at 31 medical research centers and hospitals in Canada, the Czech Republic, Israel, Italy, Poland, and the US from October 16, 2023, to June 2, 2026, among adolescents aged 12 years to younger than 18 years with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, escalated to a maximum tolerated dose (5, 10, or 15 mg), or placebo for 72 weeks, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was percent change in body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) from baseline to week 72. Key secondary end points included percentages of participants achieving BMI reductions of at least 5%, at least 10%, at least 15%, and at least 20%; changes in BMI SD score; BMI expressed as a percentage of the 95th percentile; and body weight, waist circumference, and physical functioning from baseline to week 72. Safety outcomes included treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events. RESULTS: A total of 160 participants were randomized to receive tirzepatide (n = 109) or placebo (n = 51). Mean (SD) age at baseline was 14.6 (1.6) years, 99 participants (61.9%) were female, mean body weight was 109.7 kg, and mean BMI was 38.6. At week 72, tirzepatide was associated with 18.5% reduction in BMI, compared with 0.5% increase in BMI with placebo, demonstrating superiority over placebo (estimated treatment difference, -19.0 [95% CI, -23.9 to -14.1] percentage points; P < .001). Of 10 key secondary outcomes, all demonstrated statistically significant differences favoring tirzepatide compared with placebo. Overall, 79.6% of tirzepatide-treated participants achieved BMI reduction of at least 5% compared with 28.5% of participants in the placebo group (risk difference, 51.2 [95% CI, 36.3-66.1] percentage points; P < .001). The most common adverse events with tirzepatide treatment were gastrointestinal (mostly mild to moderate). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In adolescents with obesity or overweight with obesity-related complications, tirzepatide, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention, led to significant reductions in percent change in BMI compared with placebo at 72 weeks. title: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry identifier: ACTRN12623001236684 .
